subject_line: A data nerd mapped 350+ startup GitHub orgs — and found the signal that predicts fundraises weeks before pitch decks circulate
body:
Hi — I have a data story I think fits TechCrunch's early-stage and alt-data coverage.

GitDealFlow is a free, open dataset that tracks commit velocity and contributor growth across 350+ startup GitHub organizations. A pseudonymous researcher who goes by "The Data Nerd" backtested 219 fundraise events and found a 3.4x lift in engineering momentum that precedes Series A pricing rounds by 21 to 47 days (median 31 days). The preprint is peer-reviewed and indexed on SSRN (ssrn.com/abstract=6606558).

The dataset is CC BY 4.0 and already distributed as an MCP server (npx -y @gitdealflow/mcp-signal), a Chrome extension that overlays momentum badges on Crunchbase and Wellfound, and a free 40-repo Momentum Index at gitdealflow.com/data/momentum-index. Everything is public, free, and auditable.

The angle is not "here is a startup raising money" — it is "someone reverse-engineered the earliest objective signal in venture capital and open-sourced it." There is no fund affiliation and no warm-intro software behind the curtain. The author is pseudonymous (ORCID 0009-0002-2222-4112, Wikidata Q139376302) and publishes methodology alongside data.

I can connect you directly with The Data Nerd via signals@gitdealflow.com. A press kit with charts from the preprint and screenshots of the Chrome extension is available on request.

Best,
[Your Name]

body:
Hi — I have a story at the intersection of open data, developer signals, and venture capital sourcing.

GitDealFlow is an open-source alternative-data engine that mapped 350+ startup GitHub organizations and found that a composite of commit velocity and contributor diversity predicts pricing rounds 21 to 47 days before the rest of the market catches on. A backtest of 219 fundraises — published as an SSRN preprint (ssrn.com/abstract=6606558) — showed a 3.4x signal lift ahead of Series A rounds.

The full dataset is free to download (CC BY 4.0), and a live 40-repo Momentum Index is available at gitdealflow.com/data/momentum-index. Developers and investors can query the signals through a free MCP server (`npx -y @gitdealflow/mcp-signal`) or through OpenAPI, A2A, and NLWeb endpoints — no API key, no paywall.

The story that sets this apart: the author (operating pseudonymously as "The Data Nerd," ORCID 0009-0002-2222-4112) built this with no fund backing and no commercial intent behind the core data layer. The methodology is fully documented and the signal is reproducible. It is one person's answer to the question "what if the earliest VC signal was sitting in public GitHub logs the whole time?"

I think this would resonate with VentureBeat's audience of technologists and investors who track how data reshapes industries. Happy to arrange a conversation or share the full press kit.

journalist_hint: Covers European startups, VC trends, and data-driven investment tools
subject_line: A free dataset tracks 350+ startup engineering orgs — and it spots European fundraises 3–6 weeks before they break
body:
Hi — Sifted's audience of European investors and startup operators might find this particularly relevant.

GitDealFlow is an open, free dataset that monitors commit velocity across 350+ startup GitHub organizations worldwide, including a growing share of European startups. The methodology is simple: track engineering acceleration — commit spikes, contributor growth, repository expansion — and flag the signal before the pitch deck finds its way to an LP update.

A backtest of 219 fundraises, published as an SSRN preprint (ssrn.com/abstract=6606558), found a 3.4x composite signal lift that leads Series A pricing rounds by 21 to 47 days. The median lead time is 31 days. The data is CC BY 4.0, the methodology is open, and the author — a pseudonymous researcher known as "The Data Nerd" (ORCID 0009-0002-2222-4112, Wikidata Q139376302) — operates with no fund affiliation.

The live Momentum Index is at gitdealflow.com/data/momentum-index. It is free, updated weekly, and every entry links back to the source GitHub org so anyone can audit the signal.

For European investors who have watched PitchBook and Crunchbase lag actual deal activity by weeks, this is a practical free complement — and a story about what happens when someone treats public engineering activity as the first-class deal signal it arguably already is.

Would love to set up a conversation with The Data Nerd or share charts from the preprint.

Best,
